mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of monetary regime conditions.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in >60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 0.5%, aggressive monetary tightening increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in >60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in federal funds rate and CPI inflation signal aggressive monetary policy response to high inflation, triggering short-term equity market corrections and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in >60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL rises, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.0%), labor market weakness signals reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in >60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
